subject: Agriculture
title: The Soil Food Web
description: A quick win: understand The Soil Food Web.

hook.text: A teaspoon of healthy soil contains more microorganisms than there are people on Earth.

buildup.text: Bacteria, fungi, protozoa, and nematodes form a food web underground, each eating and being eaten.

discovery.text: This web cycles nutrients. Bacteria break down organic matter; protozoa eat bacteria and release nitrogen.

twist.text: Fungicides and excess fertilizer can collapse the food web. Chemical shortcuts can kill the natural cycle.

climax.text: Soils with a thriving food web need fewer inputs. The biology does what chemicals usually replace.

punchline.text: Beneath every field, an invisible ecosystem runs the show.

quiz.question: What lives in a teaspoon of healthy soil?
options: More microorganisms than people on Earth

details.summary: The soil food web is the community of organisms living in soil—bacteria, fungi, protozoa, nematodes, arthropods, and earthworms—that decompose organic matter, cycle nutrients, and create soil structure. A healthy food web is the engine of soil fertility.
details.whyItMatters: Soil organisms cycle more nutrients to crops than any fertilizer program. A diverse, active soil food web suppresses plant diseases, improves water infiltration, and builds the organic matter that sustains long-term productivity.
takeaways: Soil contains billions of bacteria, millions of fungi, and thousands of species per gram
The food web decomposes organic matter and converts nutrients into plant-available forms
Bacterial-dominated soils favor annual crops while fungal-dominated soils favor perennials

faq.question: What organisms make up the soil food web?
faq.answer: Bacteria and fungi decompose organic matter at the base. Protozoa and bacterial-feeding nematodes eat bacteria, releasing nutrients. Fungal-feeding nematodes and microarthropods consume fungi. Predatory nematodes, beetles, and earthworms are higher-level consumers. Each group plays a unique role.

faq.question: How does a healthy soil food web benefit crop production?
faq.answer: Organisms decompose organic matter into plant-available nutrients on demand. Fungal networks transport water and phosphorus to roots. Diverse microbial communities suppress pathogens through competition. Organisms create soil aggregates that improve aeration and water infiltration.
